title: Three-Person Coupling at Equilibrium

canonical_node.axiom: The triadic-coupled system at equilibrium, with the coupling invariant, exhibits seven emergent properties that correspond to divine attributes.
definitions: Triadic-coupled system: a system of three components with a non-commutative coupling invariant, exemplified by quaternion EM.
Coupling invariant: the scalar-vector coupling in the quaternion product that is lost in Heaviside's vector reduction.
Equilibrium: the state where the system's properties are stable and self-sustaining.
Perichoresis: mutual indwelling; the coupling invariant itself.
Aseity: self-existence; the system requires no external input.
Simplicity: non-compositeness; the system is irreducible.
Omniscience: complete mutual knowledge; zero conditional entropy between persons.
Omnipotence: complete mutual actuation; perpetual mutual generation.
Immutability: time-translation invariance; the Lagrangian does not change with time.
Love as Ground State: the coupling between persons is agap; the ground state of the confinement potential.
derivation: The parent isomorphism between quaternion EM and the Trinity is Lean-verified (MaxwellTrinity.lean, zero sorry).
At equilibrium, the quaternion scalar-vector coupling is perfect and bidirectional, leading to perichoresis (T.1).
The mutual generation of E and B fields in vacuum is self-sustaining, leading to aseity (T.2).
The quaternion product cannot be decomposed into independent scalar and vector operations, leading to simplicity (T.3).
At perfect coupling, each component carries complete information about others, leading to omniscience (T.4).
The curl equations describe perpetual mutual actuation, leading to omnipotence (T.5).
Time-translation symmetry of the Lagrangian yields a conserved charge, leading to immutability (T.6).
The coupling between persons is identified with the ground state of the confinement potential, leading to love as ground state (T.7).
canonical_node.action: The system should treat the seven derived terms as proposed emergent properties of the triadic-coupled system at equilibrium, subject to further formalization and testing.
boundary: Does not push into divine mechanics (how the coupling originated, why three).
Does not claim the derived terms are Lean-verified; only the parent isomorphism is.
Does not claim the mapping from physics to theology is proven; it is structural analogy.
test: Kill condition: Show that the triadic-coupled system at equilibrium exhibits a property inconsistent with these seven terms, or that an equivalent set can emerge from non-triadic coupling, or that the coupling invariant is not load-bearing.
Open item: Formal bridge from coupling invariant to Shannon mutual information for T.4.
Open item: Formal identification of inter-person coupling with Yukawa coupling for T.7.
No Lean formalization of derivative terms yet.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a formal structure for divine attributes as emergent properties of a triadic-coupled system at equilibrium, grounded in quaternion EM.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the Lean-verified parent isomorphism and the coupling invariant.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If the coupling invariant is removed, the derived terms lose their grounding; the system reduces to Heaviside's vector EM, which is Lean-proven to lose content.

classification.recommended_atom_action: Quarantine derivative terms; keep parent isomorphism as verified.

overstatement_risks: Claiming the derived terms are Lean-verified when they are not.
Treating structural analogies as formal identities.
Overstating the strength of the mapping from physics to theology.
kill_conditions: Show inconsistency of the seven terms with the triadic-coupled system at equilibrium.
Show that non-triadic coupling can produce equivalent properties.
Show that the coupling invariant is not load-bearing.
risk.lean_target: Formalize the derivation of the seven terms from the coupling invariant in Lean 4.

plain_summary: This document proposes seven divine attributes (perichoresis, aseity, simplicity, omniscience, omnipotence, immutability, love) as emergent properties of a triadic-coupled system at equilibrium, based on the Lean-verified isomorphism between quaternion EM and the Trinity. The parent isomorphism is verified, but the derived terms are not formally proven and require further work.
